value.rationale: Random endpoint chords are a classical test of sampling bias; a near-coincidence of their midpoints has an apparently single rare-event logarithm. The marked law separates geometrically distinct long-diameter and short-chord causes in an exact 2:1 ratio and shows each has a full continuum of logarithmic scales. This conditional geometry is not captured by the known four-step marginal and gives a natural model for singular collision statistics.
